name: Janai
overview: Janai was a male chief from the tribe of Gad, recognized as a leader among the Gadites in the region of Bashan. His role as a chief highlights his position of authority and responsibility within his tribal community. Scripture mentions him specifically in 1 Chronicles 5:12, emphasizing his leadership among the Gadites.
namesAndTitles: The name Janai means 'he will answer,' reflecting a Hebrew proper name without indication of divine bestowal. This meaning may suggest attributes of responsiveness or reliability, though the text does not elaborate further.
familyAndRelationships: Janai is identified as a descendant of Gad, linking him directly to the tribe's patriarch. Beyond this tribal connection, Scripture does not record additional family relationships for Janai.
scriptureSignificance: Janai's significance lies in his leadership role as a Gadite chief in Bashan, marking him as an important figure within the tribal structure of Israel during the period recorded in 1 Chronicles. His mention underscores the organization and governance among the tribes, particularly in the region east of the Jordan River. While not a central biblical character, Janai represents the established tribal leadership sustaining Israel's community life.
